entries.title: Energy from heat inside Earth
entries.answer: Earth stays warm inside, and in some places there is hot water or steam deep underground. Wells can bring that heat to the surface. Sometimes hot water can go straight into a heating system. In some power plants, steam turns a turbine that drives an electric generator. In others, the hot water warms a second liquid that turns to gas more easily. The second gas then drives the turbine while the underground water stays apart from it.
facts: Some hot springs give a natural clue that heat from underground is close to the surface.

questions.text: Where else can we see evidence of Earth’s hot interior?
How can flowing water spin a turbine without being heated first?
What happens when a liquid becomes a gas?

entries.title: How a capacitor holds a burst of energy
entries.answer: A capacitor can hold energy by keeping opposite charges apart. Many capacitors have two pieces of metal separated by a very thin layer that does not let charge pass easily. An electric circuit can move charge so one side has more electrons and the other has fewer. If a circuit later gives the charges a path to come back together, the capacitor can supply energy for a short time. Some camera flashes use this quick release.
facts: A capacitor and a battery both store energy, but a capacitor need not use the same sort of chemical reaction.

questions.text: How does a battery use a different way to store energy?
How else can extra charges gather on one surface?
What can an electronic part do with a burst of electric current?

entries.title: How a door knows someone is coming
entries.answer: An automatic door often uses a sensor to look for movement near the entrance. Some sensors send out radio waves and notice a change when those waves bounce off a moving person. A controller then tells a motor to slide the door open. A second kind of sensing can look for someone still in the doorway, so movement alone does not decide whether it closes. The motor moves the door back when the opening is clear.
facts: Sensors can have separate jobs when they detect movement and when they look for a person remaining in a space.

questions.text: What does a sensor measure before the program chooses what to do?
How does the door get power to slide aside?
How are radio waves related to the light we can see?

entries.title: How a generator makes electric current
entries.answer: In many generators, a magnet moves past loops of wire, or the wire moves inside a magnetic field. The changing field can cause electric charges to move through the wire. The generator does not make energy out of nothing. Something has to turn it, like flowing water, a jet of steam or moving air. It changes some of the energy of that motion into electrical energy that can travel along wires.
facts: A bicycle dynamo makes electricity as the wheel turns.

questions.text: What can spin a generator using the wind?
What turns a generator inside a dam?
How can electricity make motion instead of coming from motion?

entries.title: How a heat pump moves warmth
entries.answer: A heat pump moves heat using a liquid that easily changes into a gas. The fluid absorbs heat as it becomes gas in one part of the machine. A powered pump squeezes the gas, making it hotter. In another part, the gas gives heat away and becomes liquid again. The cycle repeats. A refrigerator uses a similar cycle to take heat from the food compartment and let it out into the room.
facts: Some heat pumps can switch which side absorbs heat, so the same system can cool or warm a room.

questions.text: How can heat move from food into a cold metal coil?
How can fans help move warmth between a machine and a room?
What are liquids and gases made of?

entries.title: How a ratchet clicks in one direction
entries.answer: A ratchet has a row of teeth and a piece that catches against them. On each tooth, one face is sloped. As the wheel turns the allowed way, the small catch slides up the slope, falls into the next gap and often clicks. Turning the other way pushes the catch against the steep side of a tooth. That blocks the wheel. A ratchet wrench uses this idea so the handle can return to the starting angle between pushes.
facts: The little catch is often called a pawl.

questions.text: How can teeth send motion forward rather than hold it back?
Why does turning a threaded part make it move in or out?
What might hold a lifted load in place when the motor pauses?

entries.title: How a stovetop can heat the pan directly
entries.answer: Under the surface of an induction cooktop is a coil of wire. A changing current in the coil makes a changing magnetic field. In a suitable metal pan above it, that changing field can produce currents in the metal. The pan’s resistance turns some of the energy into heat inside the pan. It then warms food by touching it. The cooktop’s top can still become hot because the hot pan rests on it.
facts: An induction cooktop depends on both the changing magnetic field and a pan made with suitable material.

questions.text: How can one coil create an electrical effect in a second place?
What makes another heating device warm up its own metal elements?
How does water in a pan carry warmth as it moves?

entries.title: How a telescope can listen for radio waves
entries.answer: A radio telescope gathers radio waves from space. Many use a large curved metal dish that sends incoming waves toward a receiver, the way a mirror can bring visible light to a focus. An instrument changes the received waves into measurements. Scientists use them to study clouds of gas and places outside the range of ordinary cameras. A single receiver is often less useful for fine details than measurements combined from many widely separated dishes.
facts: Radio waves and visible light are both types of electromagnetic radiation.

questions.text: How do radio waves differ from light our eyes can see?
How does a telescope observe another kind of invisible light?
Why can a curved reflective surface bring rays together?

entries.title: How a tiny LED makes light
entries.answer: An LED is a small electronic part made from special solid materials. When electric current goes through it in the intended direction, charges inside can give some of their energy away as light. Different materials can produce different colors. A white LED lamp can use a coating that changes some of the light’s color so the mix looks white. Light from an LED does not depend on heating a wire until it glows.
facts: An LED still warms up a bit, even though much of the useful energy can come out as visible light.

questions.text: How can several colors of light combine on a screen?
How can one device do nearly the reverse and turn light into electric energy?
What uses electricity specifically to make something hot instead of lighting a room?

entries.title: How a tower crane lifts a heavy load
entries.answer: A tower crane lifts a load by winding a cable onto a drum. Near the hook, several lengths of cable may share the weight with a group of pulleys. The motor must move more cable, but each length takes a smaller share of the pull. A long horizontal arm can move the hook closer to or farther from the tower. Heavy counterweights on the opposite side help balance the turning force from the load.
facts: Even with counterweights, a crane can safely lift less weight when its hook is farther from the tower.

questions.text: Why does a set of pulleys need a longer length of cable?
Why does the same force turn something harder at a greater distance from its pivot?
How does where the load sits affect tipping?

entries.title: How a wedge pushes things apart
entries.answer: A wedge is thick at one end and tapers toward the other. As its narrow end moves into a gap, its sloping sides force the two surfaces apart. This changes a forward push into sideways pushes. A doorstop is a wedge that slides under the door until it presses tightly against both floor and door. Because of that pressure, each surface grips it better, so it helps hold the door in place.
facts: The thin edge of a wedge can fit where the thicker part cannot.

questions.text: What simple machine uses a ramp wrapped around a cylinder?
What keeps a pressed wedge from sliding out easily?
How do sloping surfaces help move a load another way?

entries.title: How a wheel and axle work together
entries.answer: A wheel and axle can turn as one piece even though the wheel is wider than the axle. A door knob is a good example. Pushing near the knob’s edge gives your hand a longer path to travel than the smaller axle in the middle. This makes the axle easier to turn than if you had twisted it directly. Wheels can also turn around a fixed axle, as they do in many carts, making it easier to move a load.
facts: Steering wheels and crank handles use the larger distance from the middle to give the turning force more effect.

questions.text: Why is it easier to push a lever far from its pivot?
How can a turning wheel make another wheel move faster or slower?
How can bearings let a wheel turn around a fixed axle?

entries.title: How an electromagnet turns magnetism on and off
entries.answer: When current runs through a wire, it makes a magnetic field around it. Winding the wire into a coil lets the fields of many loops work together. A piece of iron inside the coil can make that effect stronger. Some cranes use a large electromagnet to lift a load containing iron or steel. They can stop its electric current to let the load go. Electric motors and other machines use coils in different ways to make controlled movement.
facts: Magnetism made by the coil depends on current flowing in the wire.

questions.text: How do ordinary magnets push and pull even without an electric supply?
How can a changing magnetic field make a second circuit work?
How can a set of magnetic pushes make a wheel turn?

entries.title: How can a printer build an object you can pick up?
entries.answer: A 3D printer can turn a computer model into a solid object. Its program pictures the model as many very thin horizontal layers. One type of printer pushes out soft plastic to draw each layer. As the plastic cools or hardens, the next layer can join to it. Other printers build layers from powder or liquid. The object grows layer by layer, unlike a part made by carving away the material around its outline.
facts: Making a shape by adding layers is called additive manufacturing.

questions.text: How can a file describe an object with shapes and curves?
What limits the small details a flat grid of pixels can hold?
How can turning parts help move a machine tool along a path?

entries.title: How does a lever make a job easier?
entries.answer: A lever is a stiff piece that turns around a fixed point. A seesaw is a lever, and the support under its middle is the turning point, called a fulcrum. If you push down on one end, the other end goes up. Moving the turning point closer to the thing you want to lift can make the lift take less force. In return, the end you push has to move farther than the object rises. The same trade can help a crowbar lift a heavy lid.

sections.heading: Try it with a ruler
sections.text: Balance a ruler across a large eraser. Put a second eraser on one end and push gently on the other. Try moving the support toward the eraser you are lifting.

facts: A fulcrum is the point about which a lever turns.
A playground seesaw is a lever.

questions.text: What pulls the object you are trying to lift toward the ground?
How can a rope over a wheel change which way you pull?
How do tendons pull on the bones in your arm?

entries.title: How does a pulley help lift something?
entries.answer: A pulley is a wheel with a groove that guides a rope or cable. Hang one pulley from a support, run a rope over it, and tie a load to one end. You can pull down on the other end to make the load rise. That single fixed pulley changes the direction of your pull. Using more pulleys in a different arrangement can also make a big load easier to lift. The trade is that you have to pull a longer stretch of rope to raise the load the same distance.
facts: A fixed pulley can change the direction of a pull.
Some cranes use groups of pulleys to lift heavy loads.

questions.text: What other simple machine trades a longer movement for a smaller push?
Why does a raised load fall if nothing holds it up?
How do muscles and tendons create a pull inside your arm?

entries.title: How electric motors make things move
entries.answer: An electric motor makes a part turn. When electricity flows through a coil of wire, the wire makes a magnetic field. Its pushes and pulls interact with another magnetic field. The motor is arranged so the pushes keep helping the moving part turn, instead of holding it in one position. That turning can spin fan blades, drive the wheels of a model train or move the drum inside a washing machine.
facts: Some motors use permanent magnets, and some use electromagnets for both fields.

questions.text: How can the motion of a similar machine produce electricity?
How do magnetic poles push or pull each other?
How does an electric car use a motor to drive?

entries.title: How fiber optics guide a flash of light
entries.answer: A fiber-optic cable contains thin threads of glass or plastic. Light travels down a thread because its core and the layer around it bend light differently. Rays entering at the right angle bounce back inside the core and keep moving forward. A device can send a pattern of quick flashes through the fiber. At the other end, a detector changes those flashes into electrical signals. Many messages can travel in a cable at once.
facts: Doctors and engineers also use fibers to send light into hard-to-reach places.

questions.text: What happens to light where two clear materials meet?
Why does an orderly bounce preserve useful light?
How can changing light patterns carry numbers or words?

entries.title: How flowing water makes electricity
entries.answer: Water falling downhill can push blades around a wheel called a turbine. The turbine turns a generator, which sends electricity into wires. At some dams, a reservoir holds water at a higher level before it runs through a pipe to the turbine. Other stations use the flow of a river with much less stored water. Engineers consider what a dam will do to fish and the river around it as well as how much electricity it can make.
facts: Pumped storage can move water uphill when electricity is plentiful and let it flow back later.

questions.text: Can moving air turn another kind of turbine?
What turns the spinning motion into an electric current?
Why are dams built for more than one purpose?

entries.title: How liquid can push up a heavy machine
entries.answer: When you squeeze liquid in a closed set of tubes, the extra pressure is passed to other connected parts. A small push on a narrow piston makes a pressure change that is passed to a wide piston. The pressure acts across the wider area, creating a larger total push there. For that larger push, the wide piston moves less distance than the narrow one. Some lifts use this trade to raise cars so workers can look underneath.
facts: Hydraulic systems often use oil instead of water.

questions.text: Why do cars send pressure through a liquid to the wheels?
What can a pulley lift by moving a rope a longer distance?
How does water pressure affect a very different kind of structure?

entries.title: How propellers push through air
entries.answer: Each blade of a spinning propeller acts like a small wing. Its slanted shape changes the pressure around it and pushes air backward. The air pushes the propeller and the aircraft forward. The outer part of a blade moves faster around the circle than the inner part, so blades are often twisted to have different angles along their length. A similar kind of propeller can push water instead of air to move a boat.
facts: The push that drives an aircraft forward is called thrust.

questions.text: How is the blade similar to a wing that holds up a plane?
What happens if the spinning blades push mostly downward?
How can an aircraft push air back using a hot flow?

entries.title: How ships use sound to map the seafloor
entries.answer: A ship can send a short sound into the water and wait for an echo from the bottom. Sound travels at a speed that researchers can estimate from the water’s conditions. A longer wait means the sound traveled farther. The sound made a round trip, so only half that distance is the depth. Some tools send many beams at once and record them separately, helping scientists map a strip of seafloor as the ship moves.
facts: The name sonar comes from “sound navigation and ranging.”

questions.text: Why can sound return after it hits a surface?
How does a bat use echoes to find its way?
What kind of wave travels along the surface instead of as an echo deep under it?

entries.title: How solar panels make electricity
entries.answer: A solar panel is made of smaller units called cells. When light reaches a cell, it can give energy to electrons inside the material. The cell is built so that some of the moved electrons can flow through a wire and power something. Several cells linked together can supply more power than one small cell. Panels produce less on cloudy days or in shade. Spacecraft use them where enough sunlight reaches them.
facts: A solar cell can make electricity from light without a wheel or other moving part.

questions.text: Why does electricity need a path to flow through a device?
What large laboratory uses sunlight for electricity while circling Earth?
How can moving air make electricity by a different method?

entries.title: How wind turbines make electricity
entries.answer: A wind turbine turns moving air into electricity. When wind moves past the shaped blades, the difference in air pressure around them pushes them around. Their motion spins a shaft connected to a generator. Some machines change the speed with gears and others connect directly. Larger turbines often turn to face the wind and adjust their blades as the wind changes. The machines can stop when the wind is too weak or too strong.
facts: A windmill may use rotating blades to do mechanical work, such as grinding grain, without generating electricity.

questions.text: What can turn similar blades underwater?
How does a spinning generator make electricity?
Which power source can make electricity without spinning anything?

entries.title: What happens when gears mesh
entries.answer: A gear has teeth arranged around its edge. When it touches another gear, each tooth fits in a gap and pushes the other gear around. Two outer toothed wheels touching this way turn in opposite directions. If one wheel has twice as many teeth as the other, it takes twice as long to make a full turn. Builders use different gear sizes to trade speed for turning force, or to send motion through a machine.
facts: Teeth let a pair of gears carry motion without the slipping that smooth wheels could have.

questions.text: How does a chain pass motion between two wheels that never touch?
How can teeth also prevent backward motion?
What might turn the first gear in an electric toy?

entries.title: Where does a battery get its energy?
entries.answer: A battery contains materials that can react with each other. You can connect the two ends into a circuit so the reaction helps move electrons around the outside path. Inside the battery, other charged particles move through a material called an electrolyte. Together, the two movements let it supply electrical energy. A battery can only keep doing this while enough of its stored chemical energy remains. Recharging some batteries changes the materials back toward their earlier state.
facts: The ends of many batteries are marked with plus and minus signs.

questions.text: Why does a lamp need a path between both battery ends?
Where can a large battery help move a vehicle?
What other device stores electrical energy for a short burst?

entries.title: Why a ramp makes lifting easier
entries.answer: A ramp gives you a longer path to a higher place. If you lifted a box straight up, you would have to support its full weight while lifting. If you move it along a gentle ramp, the ramp supports part of the weight and you can use a smaller push over a longer distance. You still have to give the box enough energy to reach the same height, and rubbing against the ramp sometimes makes the job harder.
facts: A gentler ramp takes a longer path to reach the same height.

questions.text: How can a short ramp shape do a different job when the ramp itself moves?
How does a ramp shape fit around a screw?
How can a hanging rope make a lifting job easier?

entries.title: Why a screw moves forward when turned
entries.answer: A screw has a spiral ridge called a thread around it. Turning the screw is like moving along a ramp that has been wrapped around a rod. After one full turn, the screw moves forward by a short distance. Because your hand or screwdriver turns through a longer distance, it can make a larger push along the screw’s length. A bottle cap can also have threads, allowing it to move down against a seal as you twist it.
facts: Closely spaced threads move a screw a shorter way with each turn.

questions.text: How can a sloping surface move two things apart?
How do threads differ from teeth that are not a spiral?
How can a wide handle make turning easier?

entries.title: Why a seat belt makes stopping safer
entries.answer: When a moving car slows suddenly, the people inside are still moving forward until a force slows them too. A seat belt connects the rider to the vehicle so they slow down along with the car. A broad belt helps spread the force across stronger parts of the body. Many belt reels allow easy movement during normal riding but lock when pulled rapidly. Air bags add help in some crashes, while the belt still has an important job.
facts: A seat belt acts on a person, while the brakes mainly act on the vehicle.

questions.text: What slows the car’s wheels before the belt slows the rider?
What happens when the belt pushes back on a person?
Where does the energy of a moving object go as it comes to a stop?

entries.title: Why bicycles have different gears
entries.answer: A bicycle chain moves between toothed wheels called sprockets. A low gear makes your feet turn the pedals more times for each turn of the rear wheel. That gives you a larger turning force at the wheel for the same push on the pedals, which helps on a hill. A high gear moves the bike farther with each turn of the pedals, but each pedal stroke can feel harder. Changing gears trades distance per turn for turning force.
facts: The smallest sprocket at the pedals and a large one at the back make a low gear.

questions.text: How can teeth pass motion from one wheel to another without a chain?
What keeps the rear tire from sliding backward on a hill?
What simple machine do the wheels and their rods make?

entries.title: Why brakes press against a spinning wheel
entries.answer: In many cars, pressing the brake pedal pushes liquid through narrow tubes or controls a system that does. At a wheel, the pressure makes brake pads press on a spinning metal disc. Friction pushes against the disc’s motion, slowing the wheel. Some of the car’s stored motion energy becomes warmth in the brakes. The tires also have to grip the road, which is why stopping is harder when the road is covered in ice.
facts: Electric cars can also use their motors to slow down and recover some energy.

questions.text: How does a pressure change reach brakes at different wheels?
How can a motor recover part of the motion energy?
Why does heat spread through a warm metal disc?

entries.title: Why electric toaster wires glow
entries.answer: Inside a toaster, electric current travels through narrow heating elements. The elements resist the motion of charge, so some of the electrical energy becomes warmth in the metal. They can get hot enough to give off light and send heat toward both sides of the bread. As the outside of the bread warms, it becomes drier and browns. In a pop-up toaster, a spring can lift the bread when the heating time is over.
facts: The first electric toasters often toasted only one side at a time.

questions.text: How can warmth reach the bread without the element touching it?
What happens as the browned surface conducts warmth toward the middle?
How can a small electrical part make light without getting nearly as hot?

entries.title: Why electricity changes voltage along the way
entries.answer: A transformer normally has two coils of wire arranged around a shared piece of magnetic material. Current changing direction in the first coil makes its magnetic field change too. That changing field makes a voltage across the second coil. The number of loops in each coil helps set how much the voltage changes. Power companies use higher voltages for carrying power far along wires and then reduce it near the places that need to use the electricity.
facts: A simple transformer needs a changing current to keep producing an effect in the second coil.

questions.text: Where does a city change voltage as power moves between sets of lines?
What kind of field can a coil make when current flows?
What different machine changes motion into electrical energy?

entries.title: Why tiny rolling balls help wheels turn
entries.answer: In a machine, a wheel sometimes has to turn while a nearby part stays still. If their surfaces slide directly against each other, they can waste energy as heat and gradually wear down. A ball bearing gives them a row of small balls to roll over instead. The balls fit into grooves and spread the load around the ring. This supports the spinning part while letting it turn with a smaller amount of friction.
facts: Bearings can also use little rollers instead of balls to support a load.

questions.text: What parts of a bike wheel turn while the axle supports them?
Why does replacing sliding with rolling often help a machine move?
Where can heat go after rubbing warms metal?
